output.brief: The rejections trace to our own paperwork, not the fungicide, Lower Serra growers or Meridane. When Meridane bookings moved to the new Tallis system, the mandarin product record was copied from avocados and carried a 7.0°C carriage temperature instead of our 4.0°C spec. All five Meridane containers were sent at 7°C. The carrier's units held that setpoint closely, and our own loggers agree. All five rejected. The three Coastway containers and the first Meridane container, all set at 4°C, passed. That includes Coastway containers packed with the new fungicide, so the fungicide is not the cause. Lower Serra pallets looked worse, but those fruit were in every container and only rejected containers were surveyed, so that link is unproven. Next steps: immediately correct the temperature in the Tallis mandarin record. Have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct to 4°C. Add a check comparing reefer settings with the product spec. Hold off on suspending Lower Serra, on the cargo claim, and on reverting the fungicide. Review the Tallis setup process, including the sign-off, rather than penalising the contractor now. I'm quite confident in this diagnosis.
